target_reason: the brief mandates `@lang en`, `REFUSE` and `#ASSERT REFUSED ... BECAUSE`, which the main compiler rejects (references/dialects.md probes 01 to 04); `YMD` is rejected by main too (probe 05). check.sh is run as L4_TARGET=unstable and so makes no main comparison.

scope.encoded: Every unit of the text has a row in the coverage table of NOTES.md (436 units: 367 encoded, 21 fork, 26 inert, 22 repealed or blank in this text). Sections 1 to 26 in full, including s 1, s 14A(6), s 20(2A) to (6), s 20A, s 22(1) with its carve-out and s 22(2), s 23(2), s 23ZA, s 23A, s 23B, s 23C, s 24 and s 25(2) (the 'corresponding provision' is an explicit not-covered value). The whole of Schedule 1 as a table of 110 entries, limbs and groups (what each states, what it points at, its year or date mark), with the entries that decide something as functions (British Islands, colony, enactment, land, oath, person, writing, Rules of Court, the EU entries, offences, relationships, police: Scotland). Schedule 2 Parts I and II in full. The time module answers when an enactment comes into force (s 4, day and moment), the time standard of a time in an Act (s 9), anticipatory exercise (s 13), and refuses by name where the text is silent.
scope.inert: 26 rows, all reason 1 (not operative: front matter, cross-headings, Schedule headings and notes) or reason 2 (machinery: s 25(1), s 27). 22 rows are 'repealed or blank in this text' (dots where words were repealed, and the Schedule 3 table, which has no rows in this text).
scope.silent: The Act has no counting rule for periods of days, weeks, months or years, defines neither 'day', 'week' nor 'year', has no rule on days of rest, recess or holiday, no rule on the authority of language versions, and no rule on when subordinate legislation that says nothing comes into force. It does not say which provision of this Act corresponds to a repealed provision (s 25(2)), what s 20(4) leaves to s 20(2), or how two events on one day are ordered (Sch 2 paras 4(2), 4(3)(b), 5(a)); the days 'exit day' and 'IP completion day' and the Acts it points at are not among the sources. These are named REFUSEs or inputs, asserted by the tests.
